title: De la Place reconciles that dependence with freedom as immunity from a threefold necessity
source_text: LIII. Istam vero voluntatis a prima causa dependentiam, sic, paucis interjectis, cum ejusdem voluntatis libertate conciliat. Quomodocunque autem Voluntas nostra pendeat a Deo, ac quicquid in ea Deus operetur, constat semper illi libertas ea quam in immunitate a triplici necessitate, coactionis, determinationis a materia, & determinationis a sensu positam esse diximus.
pass_a_gloss: But that dependence of the will on the first cause, he thus, a few things being interposed, reconciles with the liberty of the same will. But howsoever our Will depends on God, and whatever God works in it, there always stands to it that liberty which we said was placed in immunity from a threefold necessity, of coaction, of determination from matter, and of determination from sense.
pass_b_english: A little further on he reconciles this dependence of the will on the first cause with the will's freedom. He writes:

'However our will may depend on God, and whatever God may work in it, it always keeps the freedom that we said lies in exemption from a threefold necessity: of coercion, of determination by matter, and of determination by the senses.'

lemmas.gloss: in immunity from a threefold necessity

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
